title: Treize sur trente-sept
subtitle: petites cellules hexagonales
dedication: pour O. — qui a lu ε avant moi.
literary_status: drafted (2026-05-06; constraint-preserving rewrite, independently audited release candidate)
literary_form: Roubaudian récit-prose; 13 thèses (MIS, romains) + 24 interstices (arabes); ~2,800 words total; edge-level lexical disjointness verified
designed_property: Triangular hexagonal patch radius R=3 (37 = 4th centered hexagonal number); 6-fold symmetry; unique MIS of size 13 forms a Star-of-David inscribed pattern (ρ=1.0, single optimum)
literary_references: Jacques Roubaud, ε (1967) — 361 sonnets organised as a Go board, ordered by an actual game; cells V and VIII quote the move 'coup soixante-treize' directly
Jacques Roubaud, La Forme d'une ville change plus vite, hélas, que le cœur des humains (1999) — short-cell prose register
Jacques Roubaud, Le Grand Incendie de Londres (1989–) — récit-prose register and architecture of branching memory
Jacques Roubaud, Quelque chose noir (1986) — elegiac short-cell register
Marcel Proust, Du côté de chez Swann — cell II opens with "Longtemps" (the first word of the Recherche), pivoting toward Roubaud's unsorted-memory rather than Proust's involuntary one

constraints.rings: 4 concentric rings = 4 tense layers (centre = présent indicatif; ring 1 = passé composé, le mois écoulé; ring 2 = imparfait, l'année qui s'achève; ring 3 = passé simple, le reste d'une vie)
constraints.wedges: 6 sectors of 60° = 6 themes on the M-axis (Mer, Mémoire, Marche, Mort, Maison, Mathématique)
constraints.edges: the graph's 90 edges enforce exact surface-token lexical exclusions: no two adjacent cells share a non-stoplisted content token under the audit method documented in notes/lexical_audit.md. This is an exact surface-token constraint after function-word filtering, not a certified French noun/verb lemma-disjointness theorem (which would require a real French POS/lemmatizer). 100% of 90 edges (90/90) discharge the constraint under the documented method.
constraints.MIS_label: the 13 MIS thèses are numbered I–XIII (Roman); the 24 non-MIS interstices are numbered 2–36 (arabic) in the gaps; the spine of the book is the unique MIS
constraints.acrostic: the first letters of the opening MIS thèses (I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII) spell O-L-I-V-I-E-R; reading them in order gives the dedicatee's name
constraints.Olivier_arc: cells V (atom 13, ring 2 imparfait) and VIII (atom 21, ring 3 passé simple) form an internal arc — the meeting through Roubaud's ε, then thirty years on, with the same marked Go move (coup 73)

reading_orders_provided: concentric (ring 0 → 1 → 2 → 3: from the moment of writing outward in time)
sectorial (one wedge at a time, six · 60°)
MIS-only spine (the 13 thèses I–XIII, in atom order, the readable book)
hex spiral (every cell once, never repeating)
paper: Jurczak 2026, arXiv (QOuLiPo: What a quantum computer sees when it reads a book)

constraints_status.audit_method: comprehensive French stop-list (function words, all conjugated forms of être/avoir/faire/aller/pouvoir/devoir/vouloir/savoir/voir, calendar terms, common adjectives) + crude stemmer; see notes/lexical_audit.md and verify with build_4_qoulipo_graphs.audit_v2 logic.
